overview: Micron Technology designs, manufactures, and sells memory and storage semiconductors — DRAM, NAND flash, and high-bandwidth memory (HBM) — serving data center, PC, mobile, automotive, and industrial customers worldwide. Headquartered in Boise, Idaho, Micron is one of only three vertically integrated DRAM makers globally (alongside Samsung and SK Hynix) and competes in NAND against Samsung, SK Hynix/Solidigm, Kioxia, and SanDisk/Western Digital. The company is in the midst of an unprecedented AI-driven memory supercycle (fiscal 2026 revenue of $133.2 billion, up from $37.4 billion in fiscal 2025), though the stock has been highly volatile since the June 2026 peak amid a broader AI-infrastructure selloff and renewed debate over memory pricing durability.

business_model.summary: Micron manufactures commodity and specialty memory chips (DRAM, NAND, HBM) and sells them to OEMs and cloud/data-center operators. Revenue is highly cyclical and price-sensitive to industry-wide supply/demand balance; the business is capital- and R&D-intensive, requiring leading-edge process nodes (1-gamma DRAM, G9 NAND) and multi-year fab construction cycles. The AI buildout has shifted mix sharply toward higher-margin, contracted data-center and HBM products, and in December 2025 Micron announced it would exit the Crucial-branded consumer retail memory/storage business entirely (wind-down completed by fiscal Q2 2026) to redirect constrained supply toward strategic data-center and enterprise customers.
business_model.customer_type: B2B — hyperscale cloud/AI datacenter operators and OEMs (smartphone, PC, auto, industrial); the Crucial B2C retail channel was exited in H1 FY2026 to prioritize strategic enterprise customers
business_model.geographic_mix: Manufacturing concentrated in the US (Idaho, Virginia), Taiwan, Japan, and Singapore; sales global with historically meaningful but declining China/Asia exposure after Micron exited China's server/critical-infrastructure market in 2023-2025 following Beijing's restrictions

competitive_position.market_position: Micron is the #2-3 global DRAM supplier (roughly in the mid-20s% share, narrowing the gap with Samsung's ~39% and competing closely with a weakened SK Hynix in some quarters) and a growing #3 NAND supplier (~15% share, behind Samsung ~28% and SK Hynix ~19%). In HBM, Micron is a fast-rising but still smaller player behind SK Hynix and Samsung, having gained share in the current cycle with HBM4 volume shipments for NVIDIA's Vera Rubin platform. In November 2026, financial media reported renewed concern over Micron's DRAM market share following its exit from the lower-margin consumer/retail segment and intensifying competition from China's state-backed CXMT, which has been raising output and, per some reports, pricing in commodity DRAM.

moat_factors.factor: Oligopoly structure / high barriers to entry
moat_factors.description: DRAM and advanced NAND require tens of billions in capex and multi-year process R&D; only three scaled DRAM makers exist globally, limiting new entrants
1-gamma DRAM node and HBM4/HBM4E roadmap keep Micron competitive on performance/bit-density, though SK Hynix and Samsung often lead on bleeding-edge HBM timing
Micron's entire calendar 2026 HBM supply is under price-and-volume agreements with customers, providing revenue visibility atypical for a commodity business
Up to $6.1B in direct CHIPS Act funding for Idaho and New York fabs lowers the cost of US capacity expansion and provides geopolitical insulation
In-house wafer fabrication, packaging, and test across DRAM/NAND/HBM supports cost position versus fabless or less-integrated peers

weaknesses: Commodity product with limited pricing power outside of supply-constrained up-cycles; historically brutal down-cycle margin collapses
Smaller HBM share than SK Hynix and Samsung, the two leaders in the fastest-growing, highest-margin memory category

Rising Chinese domestic competition (CXMT, YMTC) backed by state industrial policy is adding commodity DRAM/NAND capacity and, per some late-2026 reports, undercutting on price in markets Micron still serves
Effectively locked out of the China server/critical-infrastructure market since 2023-2025, ceding share to Samsung, SK Hynix, and domestic Chinese suppliers
High fixed-cost, high-capex manufacturing model makes margins extremely sensitive to utilization and industry-wide bit-supply growth
Heavy ongoing capex (guided above $25B in FY2026) could pressure free cash flow in a demand pullback

growth_drivers: AI/datacenter-driven HBM demand — management and industry analysts (Citi, TrendForce) forecast the HBM TAM growing from ~$35B in 2025 toward ~$100B by 2028, pulled forward by AI accelerator demand

Data center DRAM and NAND content growth — data center DRAM/NAND bit shipments in calendar 2026 expected to more than double versus two years prior, with AI/server TAM exceeding 50% of industry TAM for the first time
HBM4/HBM4E product ramp — HBM4 36GB 12H volume shipments for NVIDIA's Vera Rubin platform began in Q1 calendar 2026; HBM4E in development with 1-gamma node for calendar 2027 ramp
Capacity expansion — new/expanded fabs in Idaho (first wafer output mid-2027), New York (groundbreaking January 2026, up to four fabs over 20+ years), Taiwan (Tongluo), Japan, Singapore, and India
CHIPS Act subsidies (~$6.1B) lowering the cost of US capacity buildout and supporting domestic supply chain resilience narrative

Structural supply tightness — multiple industry forecasters (TrendForce, Citi) expect DRAM supply growth to lag demand through 2027, with HBM crowding out standard DRAM capacity; some (BofA) see a modest ASP softening in 2028 as a 'soft landing' rather than a bust
Mix shift toward higher-margin enterprise/data-center SSD and DRAM following the exit from lower-margin consumer retail (Crucial)

business.description: DRAM/NAND pricing is historically volatile with multi-year boom-bust cycles; the current AI-driven upcycle could reverse sharply if hyperscaler capex slows or supply floods the market

CXMT and other Chinese suppliers are rapidly adding DRAM/NAND capacity with state backing; November 2026 market commentary cited slipping Micron DRAM share and pricing pressure as a contributing factor in the stock's sharp pullback
SK Hynix and Samsung hold larger shares of the highest-growth, highest-margin HBM segment; losing design wins on next-gen HBM4E/HBM5 could cap Micron's upside
A growing share of revenue is tied to a handful of hyperscale/AI customers (e.g., NVIDIA platform cycles), increasing sensitivity to any single customer's capex pullback

financial.description: FY2026 capex guided above $25B; sustained heavy investment could pressure free cash flow if pricing normalizes before new capacity is amortized

Q4 FY2026 adjusted gross margin of 87% is far above historical norms; some analysts (BofA) now model a ~5-13% ASP decline across DRAM/NAND in 2028, and the stock's ~35-40% drawdown from its June 2026 high already reflects market concern about reversion

regulatory.description: Escalating and shifting US export control regimes on AI-related semiconductors (and China's retaliatory measures, including China's 2023 ban on Micron products in critical infrastructure) create ongoing uncertainty over addressable market and compliance costs

regulatory.risk: China market exclusion and domestic subsidy competition
regulatory.description: Micron has effectively exited China's server/critical-infrastructure market, ceding share to competitors and state-subsidized Chinese domestic suppliers (CXMT, YMTC), which are scaling capacity rapidly
Direct federal funding agreements carry conditions (e.g., profit-sharing above certain return thresholds, restrictions on buybacks/China expansion) that could constrain capital allocation flexibility

macro.risk: AI capex cycle dependency and sentiment risk
macro.description: A substantial portion of current growth is tied to hyperscaler AI infrastructure spending; a broad AI-stocks selloff in late October/November 2026 (driven by doubts about the durability of AI capex and memory pricing) cut Micron shares roughly 35-40% from their June 2026 peak despite still-strong fundamentals, illustrating high sentiment sensitivity

macro.risk: Global economic slowdown / PC and smartphone demand
macro.description: Non-AI end markets (PC, mobile, auto) remain cyclical and sensitive to consumer and enterprise IT spending, and Micron's exit from consumer retail removes a diversification buffer
Significant international manufacturing (Taiwan, Japan, Singapore) exposes Micron to currency fluctuations and equipment/raw material cost swings

macro_factors.industry_outlook: Memory industry remains in a historic AI-driven upcycle; data center DRAM/NAND demand is expected to more than double over two years, with HBM TAM projected to grow from ~$35B (2025) toward ~$100B (2028). Forecasters diverge on 2027-2028: TrendForce and Citi see DRAM remaining supply-constrained through 2027 (HBM crowding out standard DRAM wafer capacity), while NAND is expected to loosen somewhat in H2 2027 as new capacity and softer consumer demand catch up; BofA models a modest ~5-13% ASP pullback in 2028 as a 'soft landing' rather than a cycle bust.
macro_factors.cyclicality: High — memory is one of the most cyclical semiconductor sub-sectors, with pricing driven by industry-wide bit-supply growth versus demand. Conditions in calendar 2025-2026 were the tightest in over a decade, but November 2026 saw a sharp, sentiment-driven correction (stock down ~35-40% from its June 2026 high) even as near-term fundamentals (record Q4 FY2026 results, strong Q1 FY2027 guidance) remained strong, underscoring how quickly sentiment can swing ahead of the fundamentals
macro_factors.interest_rate_sensitivity: Moderate — high capex intensity and project financing needs make the business sensitive to borrowing costs, though current net cash position and strong FCF reduce near-term sensitivity
key_input_costs: Semiconductor fab equipment (lithography, deposition, etch tools)
Skilled fab labor and engineering talent

recent_developments.event: Announced exit from the Crucial-branded consumer memory/storage retail business globally, redirecting constrained DRAM/NAND supply to strategic data-center and enterprise customers; consumer shipments wound down by fiscal Q2 2026 (February 2026)
Broke ground on first New York fab (Clay, NY); plan includes up to four fabs over 20+ years, with supply expected from 2030 onward
Began HBM4 36GB 12H volume shipments for NVIDIA's Vera Rubin AI platform
Stock reached a 52-week closing high of roughly $1,213.56 amid peak enthusiasm for the AI memory supercycle

Reported record fiscal Q4 2026 results: revenue of $54.23B (up 379% YoY) and adjusted EPS of $33.42, beating analyst estimates; adjusted gross margin reached 87.0%; issued Q1 FY2027 guidance of $61.5B ± $1.5B revenue and adjusted EPS of $38.15 ± $1.00, both above consensus

Broad AI-infrastructure stock selloff; Micron shares fell sharply from their June 2026 peak — including a roughly 17.5% single-day drop on November 5, 2026 — on investor concern about the durability of AI capex and memory pricing, reports of slipping Micron DRAM market share, and intensifying low-cost competition from China's CXMT; shares partially rebounded (+11.9% on November 11) but remained down ~35-40% from the June high as of mid-November 2026
Director Linnie M. Haynesworth announced she will retire from Micron's board at the January 14, 2027 annual meeting

Micron scheduled to report fiscal Q1 2027 earnings; consensus estimates were roughly $61.9B revenue and $38.22 adjusted EPS heading into the print, broadly in line with management's Q4 FY2026 guidance

items.notes: Above consensus of ~$57.0B at the time; implies continued sequential growth driven by AI/data-center demand and tight supply. Next earnings report (Dec 16, 2026) will confirm whether this held despite November's sentiment-driven selloff
Above consensus of ~$35.14 at the time of issuance; reflects sustained pricing strength
Slightly below Q4 FY2026's 87.0% actual but still near record levels, reflecting continued supply-constrained pricing
Funding expansion across Taiwan (Tongluo), Idaho, New York, Japan, Singapore, and India to meet long-term AI-driven demand
Management pulled forward its TAM forecast by two years given accelerating AI accelerator demand; entire CY2026 HBM supply already under price/volume agreements

guidance.management_commentary: At the September 2026 Q4 print, management signaled that industry-wide memory supply would remain tight through fiscal 2027-2028, supporting continued pricing power and margin strength, and emphasized HBM4 volume ramp for NVIDIA's Vera Rubin platform and record data-center DRAM/SSD contributions. Since then, no updated guidance has been issued; the stock's sharp November 2026 decline reflects market skepticism about the durability of AI-driven pricing and Chinese competitive inroads rather than any disclosed change in Micron's own outlook. The December 16, 2026 Q1 FY2027 earnings report is the next scheduled checkpoint on whether guidance held.

bull_case: Historic AI-driven memory supercycle with HBM TAM forecast to grow from ~$35B to ~$100B by 2028; most forecasters (TrendForce, Citi) still see DRAM supply-constrained through 2027
Record profitability (87% adjusted gross margin, $86.8B adjusted net income in FY2026) with Q1 FY2027 guidance (issued Sept 2026) calling for further sequential growth

The November 2026 drawdown (~35-40% off the June high) has pushed valuation to a much lower forward multiple (reported forward P/E in the mid-single digits by some accounts) relative to still-strong near-term fundamentals, which bulls frame as a buying opportunity rather than a change in the earnings trajectory
Full CY2026 HBM supply already locked in under price-and-volume agreements, providing unusual revenue visibility for a historically commodity business
US-based capacity expansion (Idaho, New York) backed by ~$6.1B in CHIPS Act funding reduces geopolitical and supply-chain risk versus Asia-concentrated peers
bear_case: Memory is a deeply cyclical commodity business; the sharp, broad-based November 2026 AI-stock selloff shows how quickly sentiment on the supercycle thesis can reverse even without a confirmed change in fundamentals
Rising Chinese domestic DRAM/NAND capacity (CXMT, YMTC), backed by state industrial policy, is reportedly pressuring Micron's market share and pricing in commodity segments it still serves

Micron remains the smallest of the three scaled HBM suppliers behind SK Hynix and Samsung, risking share loss on next-generation HBM4E/HBM5 design wins in the most strategically important memory category

Heavy ongoing capex (>$25B guided for FY2026) across multiple new fabs increases execution risk and could strain free cash flow if the pricing environment normalizes before new capacity is absorbed; some analysts (BofA) already model a 2028 ASP decline
Exiting the Crucial consumer retail business removes a diversification buffer and concentrates Micron further on AI/hyperscale demand just as that end market's spending durability is being questioned

Escalating and unpredictable US-China export control policy, plus Micron's effective exclusion from China's server/critical-infrastructure market, creates ongoing geopolitical and addressable-market risk
